claim: Uncertainty-aware rollback decoding with token-level signals improves over equal-budget restart on seven code LLMs and five benchmarks, but the main gain comes from feedback-guided rollback, and no verbal, probe, random-routing, or oracle-routing arm is present.
stance_target: L3 confidence-routed budgets is NARROW; update-after-failing-test is CLEAN
scope_conditions: Token-level uncertainty signals, code generation, 7B-class code LLMs
quoted_support: A component-controlled ablation further shows that feedback-guided rollback provides the main improvement, while uncertainty localization provides an additional gain when checking, budget, rollback, and branch decay are held fixed.
numbers: gains of up to 0.26 in pass@1

breadth.confidence_families: token-level uncertainty signals only (eight signals; Max Token Entropy in the full framework, Table RQ1)
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: DeepSeek-7B, StarCoder2-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, CodeLlama-7B among seven code LLMs (Table RQ1, same-budget comparison)
breadth.benchmarks: five code generation benchmarks plus Dsec-Python (Section: datasets)
breadth.label_source: hidden unit tests; public tests used for intermediate checks (Section: separation of checks)
breadth.label_independence: public tests and hidden tests are kept separate (Experimental setup)
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present (searched: ECE, AUROC, Brier); pass@1, AvgTestPassRate, PASR
